A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DPDL research. Their text, equations, figures and tables support reliable comparison. V1's supplementary Sections 7–11 are absent from the supplied v2, which also removes the corresponding pointers; this is a document difference rather than an extraction gap.

before.justification: V1 reports original DPDL benchmark results, component ablations and parameter sensitivity analyses in Tables 1–3 and Figures 2–3, with additional class-level results in the supplement.

after.justification: V2 retains the original DPDL experiments across nine datasets, including benchmark results, ablations and sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the same Gaussian prototypes, Schrödinger bridge, prototype and dispersion losses, three prediction modules, and inference rule. Removing supplementary Algorithm 1 does not establish a change to the procedure described in Section 4.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same nine datasets under general and hard settings, including the same six dataset/subset groups in the hard-setting comparison. Removing disaggregated results does not establish removal of those categories from evaluation.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain DevNet, FLOS, SAOE, MLEP, DRA and AHL as comparators. The newly cited works do not introduce additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The reported general/hard sampling protocols, one/ten training anomalies, AUC metric, image size and training budget remain unchanged. Supplementary split and preprocessing descriptions disappear, but no replacement settings or changed experimental procedures are reported.

E4.justification: The DPL/DFL ablations in Figure 2, prediction-module ablations in Table 3, and four hyperparameter sensitivity analyses in Figure 3 are retained unchanged. The omitted supplementary tables contain disaggregated benchmark results.

E5.justification: Both Section 5.1 passages specify five independent runs, and Tables 1–3 retain mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting. Removing supplementary result rows does not change the retained uncertainty reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 removes Tables 5–6, losing MVTec AD category-level results and detailed anomaly-class results across six hard-setting dataset/subset groups. For example, Table 5's one-shot Transistor results of 0.748±0.002 for DPDL and 0.796±0.003 for AHL disappear. Retained Tables 1–3 and Figures 2–3 report unchanged results.

T1.justification: V1's Section 11 provides step-by-step derivations of the conditional Gaussian-mixture expression in Equation 13 and the bridge drift in Equation 14. V2 removes both derivations while retaining the main equations and assumptions, substantially reducing the mathematical reasoning presented.

C1.justification: The prototype-diffusion contribution, hyperspherical dispersion contribution and nine-dataset state-of-the-art claim remain unchanged in the abstract, contribution list and conclusion. The quantified performance sentence removed from the introduction remains substantively present in Section 5.4.

C2.justification: The explanations of normal-distribution compactness, generalization to unseen anomalies, component contributions and hyperparameter tradeoffs remain unchanged in Sections 5.4–5.7. V2 adds no substantive limitations or applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: V2 removes Section 7/Table 4, including dataset counts, normal-data split rules and processing details such as SDD segmentation and AITEX cropping. Supplementary pseudocode and the promised code-release URL also disappear. Main optimizer, hardware and training details remain, but reproducibility documentation is substantially reduced.

R1.justification: V2 supplies the previously missing SDD reference, adds five generative-model references with a brief related-work sentence, and attributes additional mathematical expressions to the existing LightSB references. The broader OSAD positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The document loses its entire supplementary section block and associated cross-references, changing its overall structure from main paper plus supplement to main paper alone. Retained main-text prose and section order are largely unchanged, with limited author-block, wording and footnote edits.

P2.justification: Supplementary Tables 4–6, Algorithm 1 and the extended derivation displays disappear. Main Tables 1–3 and Figures 1–3 are retained; Figure 2 moves from PDF page 8 to page 7, alongside smaller front-matter and pagination changes.

improvement.justification: V2 improves citation completeness and attribution, but removes dataset preparation and split documentation, class-level experimental evidence, pseudocode, derivations and the promised code URL. These losses substantially weaken reproducibility and readers' ability to examine the empirical and mathematical support for unchanged claims. The limited citation and editorial gains do not compensate for the missing supplementary material.
